chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I said to him, 'During the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the Mercy of his Lord.' He said: 'It means the night prayer.'
I said to him, 'And the parts of the day, so that you may be well pleased.' He said: 'It means performing voluntary prayer during the day.'
I said to him, 'And the retreat of the stars.' He said: 'Two Rak'at before the morning prayer.'
I said, 'And after the prostrations.' He said: 'Two Rak'at after the Maghrib prayer.'
ai.seo_question: What are the specific times and forms of voluntary prayer mentioned in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the practical application of Quranic temporal markers for voluntary worship, linking specific verses to distinct prayer times. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating night devotion (Qiyam al-Layl) with daytime sunnah prayers, specifically identifying the two Rak'at before Fajr and after Maghrib as key moments of spiritual connection.
